title: Extend orbit reconstruction to all discrete continuous actions
statement: Let $G$ be a topological group, and let $\mathcal O_G$, $i_G$, $\omega_G$ and $F_G$ be its open-orbit category, inclusion and underlying-set functors [def-sfb-open-orbit-functor], in compatible universes. Give both natural automorphism groups the pointwise topology [def-sfb-set-functor-aut-pointwise-topology]. Assume that the translation homomorphism $\Phi:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G)$, $\Phi(g)_U(x)=gx$, is bijective. Restriction $r:\operatorname{Aut}(F_G)\to\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G)$ along $i_G$ is an isomorphism of topological groups. Its inverse sends $\Phi(g)$ to the translation family $s\mapsto gs$ on every discrete continuous left $G$-set $S$. More precisely, for every $s\in S$, its stabilizer $U_s=\{h\in G:hs=s\}$ is open, the map $q_s:G/U_s\to S$, $hU_s\mapsto hs$, is equivariant, and $(r^{-1}\alpha)_S(s)=q_s(\alpha_{U_s}(U_s))$. Thus each extension-coordinate evaluation is this composite of an orbit-coordinate evaluation and a map between discrete sets.

proof.text: Restriction is defined componentwise: $(r\beta)_U=\beta_{G/U}$. Naturality on the orbit category follows because its arrows are equivariant maps in the full action category [def-sfb-open-orbit-functor]. Restriction preserves identity, composition and inverses componentwise, so it is a group homomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, paragraph beginning “Next, we show that ψ is injective”, especially determination on disjoint unions of G/U; returned item proof steps 10–11, conditional on orbit reconstruction.

proof.text: For $s\in S$, the stabilizer $U_s$ is a subgroup: $1s=s$, and if $hs=ks=s$ then $(hk^{-1})s=s$. The map $h\mapsto hs$ is continuous by continuity of the action, and $\{s\}$ is open because $S$ is discrete; hence $U_s$ is open. If $hU_s=kU_s$ then $k^{-1}h\in U_s$, so $hs=ks$. Thus $q_s(hU_s)=hs$ is well-defined, with $q_s(U_s)=s$ and $q_s(ahU_s)=a q_s(hU_s)$. Both sets are discrete, so this equivariant map is an arrow in the action category [def-sfb-open-orbit-functor].

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, paragraph beginning “Next, we show that ψ is injective”, especially determination on disjoint unions of G/U; returned item proof steps 10–11, conditional on orbit reconstruction.

proof.text: For $g\in G$, define $(T_g)_S(s)=gs$ on every action. Each component is a bijection with inverse $(T_{g^{-1}})_S$. For an equivariant map $f:S\to S^{\prime}$, $f(gs)=g f(s)$, which is precisely naturality for the underlying-set functor [def-sfb-open-orbit-functor]. Therefore $T_g\in\operatorname{Aut}(F_G)$. The action identities give $T_1=1$ and $T_gT_h=T_{gh}$, and restriction gives $rT_g=\Phi(g)$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, paragraph beginning “Next, we show that ψ is injective”, especially determination on disjoint unions of G/U; returned item proof steps 10–11, conditional on orbit reconstruction.

proof.text: By the assumed bijectivity of $\Phi$, each $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G)$ has a unique $g$ with $\Phi(g)=\alpha$. Put $E(\alpha)=T_g$. Step 3 gives $rE(\alpha)=\alpha$. Moreover $E(\Phi(g)\Phi(h))=E(\Phi(gh))=T_{gh}=T_gT_h$, so $E$ is multiplicative.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, paragraph beginning “Next, we show that ψ is injective”, especially determination on disjoint unions of G/U; returned item proof steps 10–11, conditional on orbit reconstruction.

proof.text: For $\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(F_G)$, naturality for the actual arrow $q_s$ of step 2 [def-sfb-open-orbit-functor] gives $\beta_S(s)=\beta_S(q_s(U_s))=q_s(\beta_{G/U_s}(U_s))=q_s((r\beta)_{U_s}(U_s))$. Thus equal restrictions imply equal values at every $(S,s)$ and hence equal natural automorphisms. Applying this to $E(r\beta)$ and $\beta$ proves $Er=1$. Taking $\beta=E\alpha$ gives the claimed coordinate formula, and step 4 gives $E(\Phi(g))_S(s)=gs$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, paragraph beginning “Next, we show that ψ is injective”, especially determination on disjoint unions of G/U; returned item proof steps 10–11, conditional on orbit reconstruction.

proof.text: The topology [def-sfb-set-functor-aut-pointwise-topology] makes each of these automorphism groups a topological group directly. At a pair $(a,b)$, to hold $(a^{\prime}b^{\prime})_X(x)=a_X(b_X(x))$ it suffices to prescribe $b^{\prime}_X(x)=b_X(x)$ and $a^{\prime}_X(b_X(x))=a_X(b_X(x))$. These are two coordinate neighbourhood conditions. To hold $(a^{\prime})^{-1}_X(x)=a^{-1}_X(x)=y$, prescribe $a^{\prime}_X(y)=x$. Taking finite intersections handles every basic neighbourhood and proves continuity of multiplication and inversion.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, paragraph beginning “Next, we show that ψ is injective”, especially determination on disjoint unions of G/U; returned item proof steps 10–11, conditional on orbit reconstruction.

proof.text: For a basic neighbourhood in $\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G)$ prescribing finitely many values $\alpha_{U_j}(x_j)=y_j$, its inverse image under $r$ prescribes exactly the finitely many values $\beta_{G/U_j}(x_j)=y_j$. It is open by the coordinate-neighbourhood description [def-sfb-set-functor-aut-pointwise-topology]. Hence $r$ is continuous.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, printed p. 64, paragraph beginning “Next, we show that ψ is injective”, especially determination on disjoint unions of G/U; returned item proof steps 10–11, conditional on orbit reconstruction.

proof.text: For a single coordinate condition $(E\alpha)_S(s)=t$, step 5 identifies its inverse image with $\{\alpha:q_s(\alpha_{U_s}(U_s))=t\}$. This is the union, over $z\in G/U_s$ with $q_s(z)=t$, of the open coordinate sets $\{\alpha:\alpha_{U_s}(U_s)=z\}$. Thus every extension-coordinate is continuous. A basic neighbourhood prescribes finitely many such coordinates [def-sfb-set-functor-aut-pointwise-topology], so its inverse image is a finite intersection of these open sets. Hence $E$ is continuous and is the continuous inverse group homomorphism required.

Source: Bhatt–Scholze, Prop. 7.1.5, printed p. 64, paragraph 'Next, we show that ψ is injective … S = ⊔ G/U_i'. The item replaces that disjoint-union decomposition with naturality at the single arrow q_s: G/U_s → S. Every argument of the parent's pre-re-split steps 10–11 (NP version) is carried here in more detail, and nothing was dropped. Step checks: (1) restriction is natural because i_G keeps all arrows. (2) U_s is open because it is the preimage of the open point {s} under h ↦ hs; q_s is well-defined, using left cosets only; q_s is an arrow between discrete continuous G-sets. (3) The translation families T_g are natural, and rT = Φ. (4) E = T∘Φ⁻¹ is multiplicative. (5) Naturality at q_s gives β_S(s) = q_s((rβ)_{U_s}(U_s)), so r is injective and E = r⁻¹ with the stated coordinate formula. (6) The pointwise topology is a group topology: two coordinate conditions for multiplication, one for inversion. (7) r is continuous. (8) E is continuous, since each coordinate preimage is a union over the fibre of q_s and basic neighbourhoods are finite intersections. Every step is honestly elementary from the two definitions and the hypothesis. Only bijectivity of Φ is used, and it is exactly what the citer's live step 4 supplies. Edge cases: trivial G, empty S, discrete ℤ, and S_3 with a non-normal stabilizer. No Hausdorff, compactness or subgroup-basis assumption is used.
